title: Routine caregiver burden screening in specialist dementia services: a systematic review separating screening from support
abstract: Objective: to assess whether routine burden screening followed by referral or support improves outcomes for family caregivers and people with dementia, separately from the effect of support itself. Methods: systematic review with studies classified by comparison and pooling within classes only. Results will follow screening.
introduction: Caregiver burden screening is widely recommended, but most evidence concerns support for caregivers already identified. Screening may also miss adult children and caregivers who do not speak the clinic's language.
methods: The hospital library searches four databases and two grey literature sources. Two reviewers screen and extract independently and classify each study as screening plus referral, support for identified caregivers, or tool accuracy. Results are extracted by relationship, gender and language where reported.
results: Screening of records has not started.
discussion: To be written against the clinic's decision on routine screening. The discussion will keep indirect evidence from support trials apart from direct evidence on screening.
limitations: Few direct studies of screening; English and Spanish reports only.
